whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant exam?

personas.label: Product-to-Cash consultants
personas.description: You lead discovery and solution design for Revenue Management, mapping business needs to catalog, pricing, contracts, orders, assets, and invoices.

personas.label: Revenue operations and delivery leads
personas.description: You coordinate scope, stakeholders, licenses, permissions, configuration, testing, deployment, and adoption for revenue projects.

personas.label: Salesforce solution consultants
personas.description: You implement product catalogs, pricing, contracts, orders, asset lifecycle, or invoice management on Salesforce’s current on-core platform.

examDifficulty.heading: What does the Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant exam cover?
examDifficulty.summary: Salesforce positions this credential for consultants who understand the Product-to-Cash lifecycle and have hands-on experience with Agentforce Revenue Management on core. The exam covers platform capabilities and implementation decisions, from product catalogs and pricing through contracts, orders, assets, and invoices.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
63% to pass, which is 38 correct answers out of 60.
Seven objective areas: platform concepts, implementation readiness, catalog management, Configure-Price-Quote, contracts and orders, asset management, and invoice management.
Implementation judgement: Match customer needs to platform features and plan trade-offs, testing, deployment, and adoption.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Organize study around Salesforce’s current exam objectives. Practise matching a customer need to standard platform features, then identify the required licenses, configuration, trade-offs, testing, and adoption steps.

examFormat.heading: Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant exam format
examFormat.intro: Salesforce lists 60 scored questions, up to five unscored questions, and a 105-minute time limit. The exam covers seven objective areas:
bestWayToPass: Check implementation readiness: Review licenses, permission sets, prerequisites, roles, scope, risks, testing, deployment, and adoption.
Structure the product catalog: Understand how categories, classifications, attributes, products, and bundles support sales needs.
Configure products and pricing: Practise product configuration, validation, pricing procedures, and accurate quotes for specific business cases.
Follow the lifecycle after quoting: Study current Contracts, Order Management, Asset Management, and Invoice Management capabilities.

certificationCard.description: This credential covers implementing Agentforce Revenue Management across the Product-to-Cash lifecycle, including catalog, pricing, contracts, orders, assets, and invoices. The guide notes that up to five questions may be unscored. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 63% pass mark, weighted towards Agentforce Revenue Management Platform Concepts and Configure, Price, Quote (18% each).

keyConcepts.h2: Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant: key topics

blocks.heading: Platform knowledge and implementation readiness
blocks.body: The current exam guide covers Revenue Management capabilities, its core data model, constraints, and trade-offs. Readiness includes checking licenses, permission sets, and feature prerequisites; assigning stakeholder responsibilities; setting project scope; identifying risks; and planning build, test, deployment, and adoption. Candidates should also understand the basic roles of Flow, Lightning page components, Context Service, OmniStudio, Business Rules Engine, and APIs.

blocks.heading: Catalog and product configuration
blocks.body: Catalog Management organizes reusable product information. Salesforce preparation material covers categories, classifications, attributes, products, and bundles. Product configuration questions may ask how the Product Configurator changes product components or attributes and validates the result. Select standard functionality that meets the stated need. See Salesforce’s [Product Catalog Management module](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/product-catalog-management-with-revenue-cloud) for learning material about products and bundles.

blocks.heading: Pricing and quote design
blocks.body: The Configure-Price-Quote objective covers the Product Configurator and pricing procedures for customer-specific cases. Translate the requirements into an accurate quote, explain the chosen pricing approach, and identify when an API or customization is needed. Salesforce’s current preparation trail includes Salesforce Pricing, Price Management, Advanced Price Management, and Transaction Management.

blocks.heading: Contracts, orders, and assets
blocks.body: The exam guide lists Contracts and Orders as an objective area and also tests Asset Management. Preparation covers digital contract management, order orchestration, and managing assets through the customer relationship. For each scenario, choose the standard contract, order, or asset capability that fits and consider the implementation and lifecycle needs.

blocks.heading: Invoices and usage-based products
blocks.body: Invoice Management is a current exam objective. Salesforce preparation materials cover billing basics, invoice automation, payment and credit management, and billing data. Usage Management covers modeling and tracking usage-based products and preparing usage data for invoicing. Match the feature to the billing or usage requirement rather than assuming a legacy object flow.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant exam
scenarioTips.intro: Use Salesforce’s current objectives to plan study across platform concepts, readiness, catalog, configuration and pricing, contracts and orders, asset management, and invoicing.

blocks.heading: Confirm implementation readiness
blocks.body: Identify required licenses, permission sets, feature prerequisites, stakeholders, scope, risks, and adoption needs before deciding what to configure.

blocks.heading: Map catalog needs to product setup
blocks.body: Connect requirements to categories, classifications, attributes, products, and bundles. Know how Product Configurator changes and validates components.

blocks.heading: Build accurate pricing and quotes
blocks.body: Choose pricing procedures for the business case. Explain trade-offs and recognize when an API or customization is needed.

blocks.heading: Trace the lifecycle after the quote
blocks.body: Place Contracts, Order Management, Asset Management, and Invoice Management in the Product-to-Cash flow. Account for fulfillment, asset lifecycle, invoices, payments, and credits as needed.

blocks.heading: Plan and explain delivery
blocks.body: Include stakeholder alignment, scope, risk, testing, deployment, and adoption. Be ready to explain why the selected standard capability fits and what constraints remain.

sampleQuestions.question: Which sequence best represents the Product-to-Cash scope of Agentforce Revenue Management?
options: Marketing journeys, email engagement, and lead nurturing
Opportunity pipeline management from qualification through close
Catalog, pricing, contracts, orders, assets, and invoices
Service case routing and customer support operations
sampleQuestions.explanation: The current exam objectives cover product catalog, Configure-Price-Quote, contracts and orders, assets, and invoice management.
whyWrong: Marketing alone does not span Product-to-Cash.
The exam covers more than opportunity pipeline management.
Service case management is not among the Product-to-Cash objectives listed.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the current Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant credential assess?
options: Marketing campaign design and email delivery
Administration of Slack workspaces and permissions
Visual styling of CRM pages and reports only
Implementing the on-core Product-to-Cash lifecycle
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce describes the role as implementing the on-core Revenue Management platform across Product-to-Cash.
whyWrong: Marketing is a different product area.
Slack administration is a separate specialty.
Page design alone is much narrower than the consultant role.

sampleQuestions.question: Which group of capabilities most closely matches the exam objectives?
options: Catalog, pricing, contracts, orders, assets, and invoices
Legacy CPQ product rules without the wider lifecycle
Marketing Cloud journeys and subscriber messaging
Sales Cloud opportunity tracking from lead to close
sampleQuestions.explanation: The exam spans catalog management, Configure-Price-Quote, contracts and orders, asset management, and invoice management.
whyWrong: The current scope is broader than legacy CPQ product rules.
Marketing Cloud journeys are outside the listed objectives.
Opportunity management alone does not cover Product-to-Cash.

sampleQuestions.question: Which capability helps model and track usage-based products for invoicing?
options: Usage Management
Sales Cloud forecasting only
Marketing Cloud Automation Studio
Chatter
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce preparation materials describe Usage Management for modeling and tracking usage-based products and preparing data for invoicing.
whyWrong: Forecasting does not model usage for invoice processing.
Automation Studio is a Marketing Cloud tool.
Chatter supports collaboration, not usage billing.

sampleQuestions.question: Which capability organizes products and bundles with categories and classifications?
options: Invoice payment processing only
Product Catalog Management
Setup Audit Trail
Email Studio
sampleQuestions.explanation: Product Catalog Management organizes product and bundle information using categories and classifications.
whyWrong: Payment processing is a later billing activity.
Setup Audit Trail logs administrative configuration changes.
Email Studio is unrelated to the product catalog.

sampleQuestions.question: What can the Product Configurator help a consultant do?
options: Configure email journeys for customer engagement
Set access permissions for every Salesforce user
Configure components and attributes, then validate
Create dashboards without using product data
sampleQuestions.explanation: The current exam guide includes configuring product components and attributes and validating the configuration.
whyWrong: Email sends are outside product configuration.
Permission sets are part of implementation readiness, not product configuration.
Dashboard design is not the Product Configurator’s purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: Which capability should a consultant consider for managing digital customer agreements?
options: Marketing Cloud Automation Studio
Setup Audit Trail
Salesforce Contracts
Chatter
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce preparation material includes contract foundations and digital contract management in the Revenue Management learning path.
whyWrong: Automation Studio is for marketing automation.
Setup Audit Trail records configuration changes.
Chatter is a collaboration tool, not a contract capability.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the role of Usage Management in the current preparation material?
options: Create email journeys for campaign audiences
Track usage-based products and prepare data for invoicing
Assign Salesforce roles and permission sets
Replace catalog management with a usage ledger
sampleQuestions.explanation: Usage Management models and tracks usage-based products and supports invoice-ready usage summaries.
whyWrong: Email journeys are not part of usage tracking.
User roles relate to access, not product usage.
Usage Management complements rather than replaces the catalog.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer needs orders orchestrated for fulfillment after a sale. Which objective is most relevant?
options: Email marketing
Subscriber data management
Service Cloud Knowledge
Order Management
sampleQuestions.explanation: The exam includes Contracts and Orders, and the learning path covers order orchestration and fulfillment.
whyWrong: Email marketing is a separate product domain.
Subscriber data is related to Marketing Cloud.
Knowledge articles do not manage order fulfillment.

sampleQuestions.question: What belongs in implementation readiness for a Revenue Management project?
options: Choose pricing before requirements are understood
Confirm licenses, prerequisites, scope, and adoption
Assume a standard product setup for every customer
Skip testing to shorten implementation time
sampleQuestions.explanation: Readiness includes licenses, permissions, feature prerequisites, roles, scope, risk, testing, deployment, and adoption.
whyWrong: Implementation details should follow requirements discovery.
Configuration should reflect the customer’s needs.
Testing is part of the delivery plan.

sampleQuestions.question: Which capability area represents products a customer owns after purchase?
options: Asset Management
Product Catalog Management alone
Business Rules Engine alone
Email Studio
sampleQuestions.explanation: Asset Management supports the lifecycle of products and services after a sale.
whyWrong: The catalog organizes products for sale; it does not track a customer’s purchased assets.
Business Rules Engine supports decisions but is not the asset lifecycle tool.
Email Studio is a Marketing Cloud product.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer needs accurate quotes for different business cases. What should the consultant configure?
options: Set pricing procedures for each business case
Configure only invoice payment options
Use free-text notes instead of product attributes
Wait until after fulfillment to set a product price
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Configure-Price-Quote objective includes configuring pricing procedures for specific cases and generating accurate quotes.
whyWrong: Invoice management is a separate downstream objective.
Structured catalog information supports product configuration.
Pricing and quote generation happen before downstream fulfillment.

sampleQuestions.question: When should an implementation use an API or customization?
options: Customize each catalog item as the default approach
Request an API whenever access permissions change
Avoid discussing the design trade-offs with stakeholders
When standard features do not meet the requirement
sampleQuestions.explanation: The guide expects candidates to recognize when an API or customization is needed and explain the requirement to a developer.
whyWrong: Custom development should be driven by requirements, not applied by default.
Permission sets alone do not require an API.
Consultants should explain trade-offs rather than avoid them.

sampleQuestions.question: Why use categories, classifications, and attributes in a product catalog?
options: Replace order management with catalog categories
Use the catalog to process invoice payments
Organize products and bundles for selling
Store marketing email performance in product attributes
sampleQuestions.explanation: These catalog structures organize products and bundles so they can be selected and configured for sale.
whyWrong: Order Management is a separate lifecycle capability.
Payment processing falls under invoice management.
Email engagement data belongs to marketing tools.

sampleQuestions.question: Which delivery work is included in the current Revenue Management Consultant exam guide?
options: Skip testing once configuration is complete
Plan discovery, risks, testing, deployment, and adoption
Focus only on custom code
Stop stakeholder alignment after producing a quote
sampleQuestions.explanation: The guide includes discovery, project planning, risk mitigation, stakeholder alignment, build, testing, deployment, and adoption.
whyWrong: Testing is part of the stated preparation scope.
The role includes platform configuration and business design, not only code.
Stakeholder alignment remains relevant throughout delivery.

sampleQuestions.question: A company sells one service at different list prices in the US and UK. What should a consultant verify first?
options: Asset lifecycle transaction rules
The order decomposition structure
The invoice document template
Price book entries by currency
sampleQuestions.explanation: The entries must carry the correct list price and currency for the selling context.
whyWrong: An asset transaction rule governs changes after the product is owned.
Order structure affects fulfillment after quoting.
An invoice template changes presentation after pricing.

sampleQuestions.question: A router requires a compatible power supply. Sellers need immediate feedback when they choose the wrong one. Where should the rule run?
options: During the invoice generation batch
During the order fulfillment request
During the asset renewal reminder
During product configuration on the quote
sampleQuestions.explanation: A configuration rule validates the choices while the seller is building the bundle.
whyWrong: Billing happens after the bundle has already been configured.
Fulfillment happens after the customer has placed the order.
A renewal reminder does not validate the initial configuration.

sampleQuestions.question: A purchased subscription is eligible for an upgrade halfway through its term. Which record represents what the customer owns today?
options: The current customer asset record
The reusable product catalog entry
The draft quote for the upgrade
The invoice from the initial sale
sampleQuestions.explanation: The asset represents the customer’s installed or subscribed product and supports lifecycle changes.
whyWrong: The catalog entry defines what can be sold to customers generally.
The draft quote represents the proposed change.
The initial invoice records billing at a point in time.

sampleQuestions.question: An approved order needs warehouse and field-installation work to run independently. Which capability coordinates the work?
options: Quote document generation
Fulfillment orchestration
Invoice posting configuration
Catalog attribute inheritance
sampleQuestions.explanation: Orchestration models the fulfillment tasks and their dependencies after the sale.
whyWrong: Quote documents present the proposed sale.
Invoice posting handles the financial document.
Attributes describe products and their configuration options.

sampleQuestions.question: Usage events reach billing without customer identifiers. What should the implementation validate before generating invoices?
options: How invoices are grouped by language, layout, and billing cycle
How selling prices are inherited across product categories
How each event is matched to its usage entitlement
How delivery orders are split across fulfillment sites
sampleQuestions.explanation: Usage must resolve to the right customer and entitlement before rated charges can be billed reliably.
whyWrong: Grouping affects invoice presentation and batching.
Product categories do not link metered activity to a subscriber.
Fulfillment routing does not assign billable usage.
